new_task_1.title: Initialize frozen attrs exceptions with a real error message
new_task_1.description: The upgrade changes `attr.exceptions.FrozenError` so frozen-instance exceptions are initialized through `AttributeError` with the message `"can't set attribute"` instead of relying on class-level `msg` and `args` attributes. This makes the exception message available through normal exception stringification and keeps `msg` aligned with the actual raised error instance.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that exceptions raised for writes to frozen attrs instances are initialized with a real exception message, so their string form and `args` consistently report `"can't set attribute"` on the raised instance.

expectation.grounded: Constructing `FrozenError` and its subclasses must call the base `AttributeError` initializer with `"can't set attribute"`, producing an instance whose `args` contains that message and whose `msg` attribute reflects the same text. Errors raised when setting or deleting attributes on frozen attrs instances should therefore expose the message through normal exception matching and string conversion.
expectation.conceptual: Frozen attrs exceptions should behave like normal Python exceptions with a real message payload on each instance, rather than depending on class attributes to describe the error.

constraints.grounded: Preserve the existing frozen-instance failure semantics and the established message text `"can't set attribute"`. The change should only affect how the exception is initialized and surfaced on the raised instance, not which operations raise or which exception classes are used.
constraints.conceptual: This fix should improve exception consistency without altering the immutability contract of frozen attrs classes.

behavior: `FrozenError` initializes `AttributeError` with the message `"can't set attribute"`.
Raised frozen-instance exceptions expose `args[0] == "can't set attribute"` on the instance.
Raised frozen-instance exceptions expose `msg == "can't set attribute"` on the instance.
String-based exception matching for frozen-instance write failures observes the same message text.
acceptance_criteria: When code triggers a `FrozenInstanceError` by assigning to a field on a frozen attrs instance, the raised exception should stringify to `"can't set attribute"` and expose that message in `args[0]`.
When code triggers a `FrozenInstanceError` by deleting a field on a frozen attrs instance, the raised exception should stringify to `"can't set attribute"` and expose that message in `args[0]`.
For raised frozen attrs exceptions, the instance `msg` attribute should equal `"can't set attribute"` and match the message stored in `args[0]`.
The upgrade should not change the exception class used for frozen-instance mutation failures.
